chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) was brought a case of a man who had hired another man to mend his door; the hired man drove a nail and the door cracked, so Amir al-Mu'minin held him liable.

key_terms.فَضَمَّنَهُ: He held him liable/liable for compensation

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling on liability for damage caused by a hired worker?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of *daman* (liability) in hired labor, illustrating that a worker is liable for damage caused to the employer's property during the repair process. It highlights the juristic distinction between direct causation and negligence, serving as a foundational text for understanding contractual obligations in Shia fiqh. The ruling underscores the worker's responsibility to exercise due care, reinforcing the ethical dimension of professional service in Islamic law.
